prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and of its biologically active form, which made incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single part, B024, with Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The round-1 exchange tested it and I think it held. The chair asked what would show that unanimity reflects relative merit and not an easy default (Sandberg's point), so I made the comparison directly. B011 has very large clinical impact but a structural credit gap, because the early chimeric receptor concept (Eshhar) is outside the supplied names and two-name or three-name versions each leave something out. B020 is a clean, mature mechanism but its translational payoff is thin. B047 and B034 are late recognitions of clinical translation whose upstream biology or antibody engineering is outside the credited names. B045 has six claimants for three places and still-early medical impact. B024 is the only candidate where the discovery chain (proglucagon processing, the active truncated peptide, glucose-dependent insulin secretion and satiety effects, the idea that this could be a drug) is complete, independently replicated and confirmed in large outcome trials, with the credited names covering separable steps. Maturity is not a concern. I would anchor the prize on the discovery of the physiology and the active peptide, since that opened the field, and say so explicitly in the citation so that it does not read as a prize for specific products.
statement.case_against: The attribution risk is still the main reservation and round 1 did not remove it. Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1(7-36) form is contested, the Habener group sits outside the supplied names, and three places force the exclusion of Lotte Bjerre Knudsen, whose acylated long-acting analogues are the drugs patients take. I no longer think it is adequate to describe her work as simply industrial, as I did in round 1, since Sandberg, Wahren-Herlenius and Svenningsson are right that half-life extension was inventive science. My reason for excluding her is narrower: the physiological and peptide-identity discoveries come first and are separable, and the three-person limit leaves no room for a fourth name. A prize that leaves out the people behind the weekly drug is a real cost and the citation should acknowledge it by wording. I also have not verified the primary papers and dates myself, so a prize built on this attribution rests on a record the committee has not fully tested.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius would keep Mojsov in the preferred configuration but treats her as the least secure slot, and would move to a Holst and Drucker pair with no substitute if a review of the primary papers fails.
responses.response: I agree that the committee should examine the primary papers and dates before the final ballot, and I would accept your fallback of Holst and Drucker as the stated contingency. I would not fill the vacant slot with Knudsen as a reflex, because that changes what the prize is about. I do disagree with the idea that B011 becomes the better prize if Mojsov fails. A narrower GLP-1 pair still rests on a complete causal chain, and B011 still lacks Eshhar. So a failed Mojsov review shrinks the B024 part but does not move me to another candidate. Until a review shows otherwise, I keep her, because the identification and synthesis of the active form is documented and necessary to everything downstream.

responses.point: Sandberg warned that near-unanimity on B024 may reflect a shared easy default, and said that calling Knudsen's work industrial understates the inventive science of half-life extension.
responses.response: Your challenge is a fair one and I tried to answer it by comparing the alternatives, as set out above. On Knudsen I now agree with you, and I withdraw my earlier mild agreement with the industrial label. Her exclusion is a consequence of discovery-level credit and the three-person ceiling, not a verdict that her contribution is lesser in kind. I take your point that a prize which includes Mojsov invites a priority argument we cannot fully resolve. I accept that risk because the alternative is to leave out the person who identified and made the active peptide, and I think that omission would be harder to defend.

responses.point: El-Manira holds that the Nobel record treats translational work as eligible, and that dropping Mojsov would leave a third place that would more naturally go to Knudsen, changing the character of the prize.
responses.response: I agree that the Nobel record treats translational work as eligible and I do not rest the exclusion of Knudsen on a rule against it. I rest it on what is distinctive to each contribution. If the committee decided the therapeutic invention was the prize, then no three-name trio would be clean, as you say. Since I think the discovery is the achievement, I keep the basic-science trio. If Mojsov fell away, I agree with you that Knudsen is the natural third name, but I would prefer to take that decision openly in a further round and not as an automatic substitution. I also continue to prefer B020 as a stand-alone future prize and not a second part here.

responses.point: Linnarsson regards Rosenberg's omission and the missing Eshhar credit as the reason B011 carries more attribution risk than the GLP-1 trio, and holds B047 and B011 as fallbacks.
responses.response: I agree that the Eshhar gap is the main structural obstacle for B011, and it is why I keep it as an alternative and not a second part. The June and Sadelain pair is the cleaner form, and a citation narrowed to costimulated CARs can be defended, but only if the committee says openly that the origin of the chimeric receptor is not being credited. On B047 I stay where I was. The decisive clinical proof is real, but the upstream BCR-ABL genetics sit outside Lydon, Druker and Sawyers, and its recognition through earlier prizes weakens it as a fallback compared with B011.

responses.point: The chair asked whether a second part should be tested, noting that a second part forces a worse trio under the three-person limit, and asked how Perlmann and El-Manira differ on pairing B020 with B024.
responses.response: I looked again at pairing B020 with B024 and my answer is no. A second part would put Walter and Mori next to three GLP-1 names, which is five people and breaks the limit. Cutting the GLP-1 side to two to make room would damage the strongest part to add a weaker one. I hold B020 in reserve because the Walter and Mori pair is clean and mature, but Ron's PERK and integrated stress response work is not on the supplied list, so the citation bound is less clear than I first accepted, and the translational payoff remains thin. My difference with El-Manira is small: we both rate it highly as a stand-alone future prize. I also hold to my view that if the committee wants to honour drug development, it should be a separate achievement and not a dilution of this one.

uncertainties: Whether the primary papers and dates support crediting Mojsov for the active GLP-1(7-36) form alongside Holst and Drucker, given the Habener group's parallel work. I have not verified this beyond the supplied credit lists.

Whether the committee will accept a citation anchored on physiology and the active peptide, or whether it will insist that drug development be recognised, in which case Knudsen would need a place and one of the three would have to give way.
If the Mojsov review fails, whether the right response is a Holst and Drucker pair or a restructured trio including Knudsen. I lean to the pair but have not settled it.
Whether the B011 attribution gap (Eshhar and early chimeric receptor work) could be closed by a narrow citation, which would matter only if B024 stalls.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict is apparent between me and any credited name on B024, B011 or B020. My nuclear-receptor work with Ronald Evans and my dopamine-neuron research do not overlap with these candidates. As previously disclosed, I have co-authored with Per Svenningsson and, once (2009), with Abdel El Manira, on matters unrelated to any shortlisted candidate. I also serve as Secretary of the committee and the Assembly, and I read my role in this simulation as that of a voting member under the shared protocol. Nothing in round 1 changes these disclosures.
